title: How to change cursor in Zoom on Mac: simple steps for better meeting visibility
metaTitle: How to change cursor in Zoom on Mac: Easy Visibility Tips
description: Learn how to change cursor in Zoom on Mac. Follow these steps to adjust your pointer size or highlight your mouse for better visibility during presentations.
intro: You cannot change the cursor directly within Zoom settings, but you can adjust your Mac system pointer or use Zoom annotation tools to highlight it. These methods ensure your mouse remains visible to participants during screen sharing sessions.
tldr: Adjust your system-wide cursor size in macOS System Settings for a permanent change.
Use the Zoom Annotate tool to turn your mouse into a spotlight or arrow during meetings.
Ensure your Zoom desktop client is updated to version 5.3.1 or higher for the best experience.
Check your display resolution if your cursor appears smaller than expected while sharing.

stats.label: Minimum version for advanced cursor features

blocks.text: Why adjust your cursor for Zoom meetings

High resolution displays make small cursors difficult to follow. When you share your screen, participants often struggle to track your movements. Making your cursor larger or adding a highlight helps your audience focus on the specific buttons or data you are explaining. This simple adjustment reduces eye strain for everyone involved in your presentation.
Change cursor in Zoom using macOS settings

The most reliable way to change how your pointer looks is through your Mac system settings. This change affects your entire computer, not just Zoom. It is the best way to ensure your cursor is always visible regardless of the app you are using.

items: Click the Apple icon in the top left corner of your screen.
Select System Settings from the menu.
Navigate to the Accessibility section in the sidebar.
Click on Display to see your pointer options.
Adjust the Pointer size slider to your preferred level.
Use the Pointer outline color or Pointer fill color options to pick a high contrast shade.

blocks.text: Once you make these changes, they apply immediately. You do not need to restart your computer or Zoom. Your viewers will see this larger, colored cursor whenever you share your screen.
Highlight your mouse during screen sharing

If you only want to highlight your cursor while presenting, use the built-in Zoom annotation tools. This is useful for product demos or teaching, as it adds a visual indicator to your mouse only when you need it.

items: Start or join your Zoom meeting.
Click the Share Screen button and select your window.
Look for the floating meeting toolbar at the top or bottom of your screen.
Click the Annotate button to open the toolbar.
Select the Spotlight icon from the menu.
Choose the red dot or arrow option to highlight your pointer.

blocks.text: When you are done, simply click your mouse to exit the highlight mode. This keeps your screen clean during regular conversation and only enables the pointer effect when you are actively demonstrating something.

Sometimes your cursor might look smaller than expected while sharing. This usually happens because of screen resolution scaling. If your viewers complain that they cannot see your mouse, check the Zoom view options.

Click View Options at the top of your meeting window. Ensure the Zoom ratio is set to 100 percent or higher. If you are using a very high resolution display, the system might be shrinking the content to fit the window, which also scales down the cursor.
Third party tools for cursor customization

Some users prefer animated or custom shaped cursors. macOS does not natively support these. Applications like Mousecape allow for more customization, but they do not integrate directly with Zoom. If you use these tools, your cursor might look different to you, but it will likely revert to the default system cursor when you share your screen with others.

Visibility is the goal. Use a high contrast color like bright yellow or red for your cursor. Avoid white or light gray if you frequently share slides with light backgrounds. Test your cursor visibility in a private meeting before your actual presentation to see how it looks from the attendee perspective.
Maintaining your Mac for Zoom performance

Zoom performance relies on your Mac being up to date. Always run the latest version of macOS. This ensures that accessibility features like cursor customization work as expected. If you experience lag while using annotation tools, close unnecessary background apps to free up system resources.

faq.question: Can I change the cursor color only for Zoom?
faq.answer: No, macOS system settings apply the cursor color change globally. It will change the cursor appearance for all applications on your Mac.

faq.question: Why is my cursor small during Zoom screen sharing?
faq.answer: This is often due to screen resolution settings. Check your Zoom view ratio and ensure it is set to 100 percent or higher.

faq.question: Do I need special software to highlight my mouse in Zoom?
faq.answer: No, you can use the built-in Annotate tool in the Zoom meeting toolbar to turn your cursor into a spotlight or arrow.

steps.name: Adjust system pointer size
steps.text: Open System Settings, go to Accessibility, then Display, and move the pointer size slider to increase visibility.

steps.name: Enable cursor spotlight
steps.text: During a screen share, click Annotate in the Zoom toolbar, select Spotlight, and choose the red dot or arrow.

troubleshooting.problem: Cursor size reverts when sharing screen
troubleshooting.fix: Check your Zoom view ratio and set it to 100 percent or higher.
Ensure you are actively sharing your screen and that the host has enabled annotation permissions.
